statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-26646 (GHSA-h4j7-5rxr-p4wc) is a .NET SDK and MSBuild spoofing issue: external control of a file name or path in the MSBuild DownloadFile task. Microsoft lists .NET 9.0.105 SDK, 9.0.203 SDK and earlier as affected, and Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Core up to 17.8.3, 17.10.4, 17.11.4, 17.12.6 and 17.13.9 as affected, with 17.12.36 as the patched version on the 17.12 line (https://github.com/dotnet/msbuild/security/advisories/GHSA-h4j7-5rxr-p4wc, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/356). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: every build carries .NET SDK 9.0.113 or later in dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap, and every implementation copy of Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Core.dll, in that SDK (including its F# and dotnet-format copies) and in the Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Core NuGet package in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts, has file version 17.12.53 or later. The Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Core 17.3.4 that scanners report is one of the source-build reference packages in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts (versions 16.8.0, 17.3.4, 17.4.0, 17.8.3, 17.8.29 and 17.8.43), which hold only reference assemblies, API signatures with no implementation (https://github.com/dotnet/source-build-reference-packages), so they carry no DownloadFile code. Every published build carries the fix, so the range ends at 9.0.12-r0, the lowest published build.

CVE-2025-26646 (GHSA-h4j7-5rxr-p4wc) is a .NET SDK and MSBuild spoofing issue: external control of a file name or path in the MSBuild DownloadFile task. Microsoft lists .NET 9.0.105 SDK, 9.0.203 SDK and earlier as affected, and Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Core up to 17.8.3, 17.10.4, 17.11.4, 17.12.6 and 17.13.9 as affected, with 17.12.36 as the patched version on the 17.12 line (https://github.com/dotnet/msbuild/security/advisories/GHSA-h4j7-5rxr-p4wc, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/356). DHI dotnet9-sdk is the .NET 9 SDK built for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the SDK version it carries. Scanned all 176 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.113-r0, 9.0.114-r0, 9.0.115-r0, 9.0.116-r0, 9.0.117-r0, 9.0.118-r0, 9.0.119-r0, 9.0.121-r0, 9.0.122-r0, 9.0.123-r0 and 9.0.124-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold. Each build's SDK ships exactly three copies of Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Core.dll (the SDK's own, and the F# and dotnet-format copies), all with the same file version: 17.12.53 in 9.0.113, 17.12.55 in 9.0.114, 17.12.57 in 9.0.115 through 9.0.123, and 17.12.77 in 9.0.124, all at or above the patched 17.12.36. No package carries a Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Core 17.3.4 assembly or NuGet package. The 17.3.4 that scanners report comes from dependency entries in the .deps.json files of Roslyn's Microsoft.Build.Tasks.CodeAnalysis and of the MSBuild build host used by dotnet-format and dotnet-watch, checked in 9.0.113-r0 and 9.0.124-r0. None of those directories ships its own Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Core.dll, so they use the SDK's 17.12 copy. Every published build carries the fix, so the range ends at 9.0.113-r0, the lowest published build.
